m.x: Returns all items stored in the RTree as a flat array.

r.x: An array containing all items currently stored in the tree.

m.x: Removes all items from the RTree, resetting it to an empty state.

Tests whether any item in the RTree intersects with the given bounding box. Unlike `search`, this method stops as soon as the first intersection is found, making it more efficient when you only need to know whether a collision exists rather than retrieving all results.

p.x: The bounding box to test against. Must have `minX`, `minY`, `maxX`, and `maxY` properties.

r.x: `true` if any item in the tree intersects with the bounding box, otherwise `false`.

m.x: Comparator function used to sort items by their minimum X boundary (`left` property). Returns a negative number if `a` should sort before `b`, a positive number if after, or zero if equal.

r.x: The difference between the `left` values of the two items.

m.x: Comparator function used to sort items by their minimum Y boundary (`top` property). Returns a negative number if `a` should sort before `b`, a positive number if after, or zero if equal.

r.x: The difference between the `top` values of the two items.

m.x: Populates this RTree with data previously exported via `toJSON`. This allows a tree to be serialized and restored without re-inserting every item individually.

p.x: The tree data to import, as returned by `toJSON`.

m.x: Inserts a single item into the RTree.

p.x: The item to insert. Must have `left`, `top`, `right`, and `bottom` properties.

m.x: Bulk loads an array of items into the RTree. Bulk loading is significantly more efficient than inserting items one by one when adding large datasets, as it builds an optimally structured tree in a single pass using the OMT algorithm. If the array is smaller than the minimum entry threshold, items are inserted individually instead.

p.x: An array of items to insert. Each item must have `left`, `top`, `right`, and `bottom` properties.

m.x: Removes a single item from the RTree. An optional equality function can be provided to compare items by value rather than by reference, which is useful when the original item reference is not available. The function receives two items and should return `true` if they are considered equal.

p.x: An optional custom equality function taking two items and returning a boolean.

m.x: Searches the RTree for all items that intersect with the given bounding box and returns them as an array.

p.x: The bounding box to search within. Must have `minX`, `minY`, `maxX`, and `maxY` properties.

r.x: An array of all items in the tree that intersect with the given bounding box.

m.x: Converts a Phaser-style bounds object into the internal bounding box format used by the RTree. Maps the `left`, `top`, `right`, and `bottom` properties of the input to `minX`, `minY`, `maxX`, and `maxY` respectively, which is the format expected by the R-tree algorithms.

p.x: The object to convert. Must have `left`, `top`, `right`, and `bottom` properties.

r.x: A bounding box object with `minX`, `minY`, `maxX`, and `maxY` properties.

m.x: Returns the raw internal tree data as a JSON-compatible object. The returned value can be passed to `fromJSON` to restore the tree state at a later point.
